q: Which AWS service is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages?

opts.b: AWS CodeBuild

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit is a source control service, not a build service.
exp.b: Correct. AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed CI service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces deployable artifacts.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeDeploy handles deployments, not building.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodePipeline orchestrates the workflow but doesn't build code.

q: What is the primary function of AWS CodePipeline?

opts.b: Build and test applications

exp.a: Incorrect. Storing source code is CodeCommit's role.
exp.b: Incorrect. Building and testing is CodeBuild's role.
exp.c: Correct. CodePipeline automates the steps required to release software changes by orchestrating build, test, and deploy phases.
exp.d: Incorrect. Deploying to EC2 is CodeDeploy's role.

q: What type of compute targets does CodeDeploy support for deployment?

opts.b: EC2 instances, on-premises servers, Lambda functions, and ECS services

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeDeploy supports more than just EC2.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports deployment to EC2 instances, on-premises servers, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon ECS services.
exp.c: Incorrect. Lambda is only one of several supported targets.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 is not a CodeDeploy deployment target.

q: Which file does CodeBuild use to define build instructions?

opts.b: Dockerfile

exp.a: Incorrect. appspec.yml is used by CodeDeploy.
exp.b: Incorrect. Dockerfile is for building container images.
exp.c: Correct. buildspec.yml defines the build phases, environment variables, artifacts, and reports for CodeBuild.
exp.d: Incorrect. template.yaml is typically used for CloudFormation/SAM templates.

q: What is the minimum number of stages required in a CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. A single stage is not enough for a valid pipeline.
exp.b: Correct. A CodePipeline requires a minimum of 2 stages (e.g., Source and Build, or Source and Deploy).
exp.c: Incorrect. While common, 3 stages is not the minimum requirement.
exp.d: Incorrect. 4 stages exceed the minimum requirement.

q: A developer wants to store their company's application code in AWS with version control and without managing any servers. Which service should they use?

opts.b: AWS CodeCommit

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 versioning tracks file versions but doesn't provide Git-based source control.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit is a fully managed, serverless Git repository service ideal for storing application code with version control.
exp.c: Incorrect. EBS is block storage for EC2 instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. Storage Gateway is for hybrid storage, not source control.

q: What does the 'Source' stage in CodePipeline do?

opts.b: Deploys the application
opts.c: Detects changes in the source repository and retrieves the latest code

exp.a: Incorrect. Compilation happens in the Build stage.
exp.b: Incorrect. Deployment happens in the Deploy stage.
exp.c: Correct. The Source stage detects changes in the configured source provider (CodeCommit, GitHub, S3, etc.) and retrieves the source code for subsequent stages.
exp.d: Incorrect. Testing typically occurs in a Build or Test stage.

q: Which AWS service is used to automate code deployments to any instance, including EC2 and on-premises servers?

opts.b: AWS CodeDeploy

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudFormation provisions infrastructure, not application deployments.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy automates code deployments to EC2 instances, on-premises instances, Lambda, and ECS.
exp.c: Incorrect. Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS that handles deployment but with less granular control.
exp.d: Incorrect. OpsWorks uses Chef/Puppet for configuration management.

q: In CodeDeploy, what is an 'application'?

opts.a: The software you want to deploy
opts.b: A name that uniquely identifies the application to be deployed, acting as a container for deployment groups and revisions
opts.c: An EC2 instance running the application

exp.a: Incorrect. While related, the application in CodeDeploy is a logical container, not the software itself.
exp.b: Correct. A CodeDeploy application is a logical name that serves as a container for deployment groups, revisions, and deployment configurations.
exp.c: Incorrect. EC2 instances are targets, not applications.
exp.d: Incorrect. Build outputs are revisions, not applications.

q: What is a 'deployment group' in CodeDeploy?

opts.a: A group of IAM users who can perform deployments
opts.b: A set of instances or Lambda functions targeted for deployment, along with deployment settings

exp.a: Incorrect. Deployment groups contain target instances, not IAM users.
exp.b: Correct. A deployment group defines the target instances (identified by tags or Auto Scaling groups), deployment configuration, load balancer info, and rollback settings.
exp.c: Incorrect. Scripts are part of the revision, not the deployment group.
exp.d: Incorrect. Deployment groups are technical configurations, not team structures.

q: A team wants to automatically build their Java application whenever code is pushed to the main branch. They don't want to manage any build servers. Which service should they use?

opts.b: AWS CodeBuild

exp.a: Incorrect. Jenkins on EC2 requires managing build servers.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild is fully managed—no servers to provision, patch, or scale. It automatically scales to meet build demands.
exp.c: Incorrect. Lambda has time and size limits making it unsuitable for full application builds.
exp.d: Incorrect. EC2 with Maven requires server management.

q: Which section of buildspec.yml defines the commands to run during the build?

opts.b: phases

exp.a: Incorrect. The env section defines environment variables.
exp.b: Correct. The phases section contains install, pre_build, build, and post_build phases where you define commands to execute.
exp.c: Incorrect. The artifacts section defines output files.
exp.d: Incorrect. The reports section defines test report configurations.

q: A startup wants to set up a complete CI/CD pipeline on AWS. Their workflow is: pull code from GitHub → build and test → deploy to EC2. Which services should they use?

opts.b: CodeCommit + Lambda + CloudFormation

exp.a: Correct. CodePipeline orchestrates the flow with GitHub as the source, CodeBuild handles building and testing, and CodeDeploy deploys to EC2 instances.
exp.b: Incorrect. CodeCommit is unnecessary if using GitHub; Lambda isn't a build service.
exp.c: Incorrect. These services don't form a CI/CD pipeline.
exp.d: Incorrect. Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS and doesn't provide the same granular CI/CD control.

q: What does CodeDeploy use to identify which EC2 instances belong to a deployment group?

opts.b: Tags or Auto Scaling groups

exp.a: Incorrect. Instance IDs are not the primary identification method.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy identifies target instances using EC2 tags (key-value pairs) or Auto Scaling group names.
exp.c: Incorrect. IP addresses are not used to identify deployment targets.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security groups define network access, not deployment targeting.

q: How does CodeBuild charge you?

opts.b: Per build minute based on compute type

exp.a: Incorrect. Per-repository pricing is for CodeCommit.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild charges per minute of build time, and the rate varies based on the compute type (small, medium, large, 2xlarge).
exp.c: Incorrect. There's no flat monthly fee for CodeBuild.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lines of code is not a billing metric.

q: Is there a charge for CodeDeploy when deploying to EC2 or on-premises instances?

opts.b: No, deployments to EC2/on-premises are free; charges only apply for Lambda and ECS deployments
opts.c: Yes, based on number of instances
opts.d: No, CodeDeploy is completely free for all targets

exp.a: Incorrect. EC2/on-premises deployments are not charged per deployment.
exp.b: Correct. There is no additional charge for CodeDeploy deployments to EC2 or on-premises instances. However, deployments to Lambda or ECS are charged per deployment.
exp.c: Incorrect. There's no per-instance charge for EC2 deployments.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda and ECS deployments do incur charges.

q: A team wants to prevent direct pushes to the 'main' branch in CodeCommit and require all changes through pull requests. How can they achieve this?

opts.b: Use IAM policies with conditions to deny push actions on the main branch
opts.c: Create a separate repository for the main branch

exp.a: Incorrect. Deleting main branch eliminates the production code.
exp.b: Correct. IAM policies with conditions (using codecommit:References) can deny direct push/merge to specific branches while allowing pull request merges.
exp.c: Incorrect. Separate repositories don't solve the branch protection problem.
exp.d: Incorrect. HTTPS vs SSH doesn't control branch permissions.

q: What happens if a CodeBuild build exceeds its configured timeout?

opts.b: The build is marked as failed and stopped
opts.c: The build is paused and can be resumed
opts.d: An additional hour is automatically added

exp.a: Incorrect. Builds are stopped when they exceed the timeout.
exp.b: Correct. When a build exceeds the configured timeout, CodeBuild stops the build and marks it as TIMED_OUT (failed).
exp.c: Incorrect. Builds cannot be paused and resumed.
exp.d: Incorrect. No additional time is automatically granted.

q: What is the default build timeout for a CodeBuild project?

opts.b: 60 minutes

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 minutes is below the default.
exp.b: Correct. The default build timeout for CodeBuild is 60 minutes (1 hour).
exp.c: Incorrect. 120 minutes exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 480 minutes is the maximum, not the default.

q: A team deployed a new version using CodeDeploy but the application is crashing. They need to quickly revert to the previous version. What should they do?

opts.a: Manually copy old files back to the server
opts.b: Use CodeDeploy's rollback feature which deploys the last known good revision
opts.d: Terminate the instance and launch a new one

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual file copying is error-prone and not automated.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports rollback by deploying the last known good revision. This can be triggered manually or configured for automatic rollback on failure.
exp.c: Incorrect. EC2 snapshots are a heavier solution and may not contain the latest data.
exp.d: Incorrect. Terminating instances is disruptive and unnecessary.

q: Which CodeDeploy deployment configuration sends traffic to all instances at once?

opts.b: HalfAtATime

exp.a: Incorrect. OneAtATime deploys to instances sequentially.
exp.b: Incorrect. HalfAtATime deploys to half the fleet at a time.
exp.c: Correct. AllAtOnce attempts to deploy to all instances simultaneously, making it the fastest but riskiest option.
exp.d: Incorrect. Linear is for gradual Lambda/ECS traffic shifting.

q: What IAM entity does CodeBuild use to access AWS resources during a build?

opts.b: IAM service role

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM users are not recommended for service access.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild uses an IAM service role (trust policy allows codebuild.amazonaws.com) to access AWS resources like S3, ECR, Secrets Manager, etc.
exp.c: Incorrect. Root account should never be used for service operations.
exp.d: Incorrect. Storing access keys in buildspec.yml is a security anti-pattern.

q: A team notices that their CodePipeline stops at the Deploy stage showing 'Action execution failed'. The error mentions a missing IAM permission. What should they check?

opts.b: The CodePipeline service role permissions for the deploy action

exp.a: Incorrect. Repository permissions affect the Source stage, not Deploy.
exp.b: Correct. The CodePipeline service role must have permissions to interact with the deployment service (e.g., codedeploy:CreateDeployment). Missing permissions in this role cause deploy action failures.
exp.c: Incorrect. Pipeline actions use the service role, not individual developer permissions.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security groups affect network access, not IAM permissions.

q: Can CodeCommit repositories be replicated across AWS regions?

opts.b: No, but you can set up cross-region replication manually using triggers and Lambda

exp.a: Incorrect. AWS doesn't automatically replicate CodeCommit repositories.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit doesn't have built-in cross-region replication, but you can implement it using CodeCommit triggers, Lambda functions, or EventBridge rules to push changes to a repository in another region.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 CRR doesn't apply to CodeCommit repositories.
exp.d: Incorrect. It is possible with custom automation.

q: What is a CodeDeploy 'revision'?

opts.a: A version of the deployment configuration
opts.b: A version of the content (source code, scripts, config files) to be deployed along with the appspec.yml file
opts.d: A version of the CodeDeploy agent

exp.a: Incorrect. Deployment configurations are separate from revisions.
exp.b: Correct. A revision includes the application source code, deployment scripts, configuration files, and the appspec.yml file—everything needed to deploy the application.
exp.c: Incorrect. While a Git commit may be the source, the revision is the deployable bundle.
exp.d: Incorrect. Agent versions are not revisions.

q: Your CodeBuild project needs to access an npm private registry using an authentication token. Where should you securely store this token?

opts.b: Store in AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference it in buildspec.yml env section
opts.c: Store it in a public S3 bucket
opts.d: Pass it as a Git commit message

exp.a: Incorrect. Hardcoding secrets in buildspec.yml is a security risk as it's stored in source control.
exp.b: Correct. Use Secrets Manager or Parameter Store SecureString for secure storage. Reference them in the buildspec.yml env/secrets-manager or env/parameter-store section.
exp.c: Incorrect. Public S3 buckets expose secrets to everyone.
exp.d: Incorrect. Commit messages are visible in Git history.

q: What triggers a CodePipeline execution when using CodeCommit as a source?

opts.b: Amazon EventBridge rule detecting repository changes

exp.a: Incorrect. While manual triggers work, automatic triggers are the primary mechanism.
exp.b: Correct. When CodeCommit is the source, an Amazon EventBridge rule detects push events to the configured branch and automatically triggers the pipeline execution.
exp.c: Incorrect. Cron schedules are possible but not the default trigger mechanism.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch metric alarms don't trigger pipeline executions.

q: What CodePipeline stage type requires human intervention before proceeding?

opts.b: Build

exp.a: Incorrect. Source stages are automatic.
exp.b: Incorrect. Build stages run automatically.
exp.c: Correct. Manual Approval actions pause the pipeline and require a human to approve or reject before the pipeline continues to the next stage.
exp.d: Incorrect. Deploy stages execute automatically unless preceded by an approval.

q: A team has 5 EC2 instances running their application. They want to deploy with minimal downtime, deploying to half the fleet at a time. Which CodeDeploy configuration should they use?

opts.b: CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime

exp.a: Incorrect. AllAtOnce deploys to all instances simultaneously, causing maximum downtime.
exp.b: Correct. HalfAtATime deploys to half the instances while the other half continues serving traffic, then deploys to the remaining half, reducing downtime.
exp.c: Incorrect. OneAtATime is the safest but slowest option.
exp.d: Incorrect. Linear50Percent is not a standard EC2 deployment configuration name.

q: What happens to a CodePipeline if the source action fails?

opts.a: The pipeline skips to the deploy stage
opts.b: The entire pipeline execution fails and no subsequent stages run
opts.d: The pipeline uses the last successful source

exp.a: Incorrect. Stages cannot be skipped when a preceding stage fails.
exp.b: Correct. If the source action fails, the pipeline execution is marked as failed and no downstream stages execute.
exp.c: Incorrect. Automatic retries are not the default behavior for source actions.
exp.d: Incorrect. Each execution must successfully retrieve source code.

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid phase in CodeBuild's buildspec.yml?

opts.b: pre_build

exp.a: Incorrect. install is a valid phase for installing dependencies.
exp.b: Incorrect. pre_build is a valid phase for pre-build commands.
exp.c: Correct. 'compile' is NOT a valid buildspec phase. The valid phases are: install, pre_build, build, and post_build.
exp.d: Incorrect. post_build is a valid phase for post-build commands.

q: A company wants to see build status directly on their GitHub repository README. Which CodeBuild feature enables this?

opts.b: Build badges

exp.a: Incorrect. SNS notifications alert users but don't display on GitHub.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild build badges provide an embeddable URL that displays the latest build status (passing/failing) which can be embedded in a GitHub README.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch dashboards are for AWS Console viewing.
exp.d: Incorrect. Build reports show test details, not embeddable status badges.

q: What is the purpose of the 'artifacts' section in buildspec.yml?

opts.b: To define which output files should be uploaded to S3 after the build completes

exp.a: Incorrect. Input files come from the source, not the artifacts section.
exp.b: Correct. The artifacts section specifies which files from the build should be uploaded to the S3 output bucket, including file paths, base-directory, and naming.
exp.c: Incorrect. Environment variables are in the env section.
exp.d: Incorrect. Docker images are specified in the project environment configuration.

q: A developer notices that CodeBuild logs are not appearing in CloudWatch Logs. What is the most likely issue?

opts.a: CloudWatch Logs is not supported by CodeBuild
opts.b: The CodeBuild service role is missing the logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, and logs:PutLogEvents permissions
opts.c: CloudWatch Logs must be in the same VPC as CodeBuild
opts.d: Logs are only available in S3

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild supports CloudWatch Logs integration.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeBuild service role needs CloudWatch Logs permissions (logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents) to write build logs.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs doesn't require VPC configuration.
exp.d: Incorrect. Logs can go to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or both.

q: CodeCommit repositories can trigger notifications to which AWS service when events occur (like push, pull request creation)?

opts.b: Amazon SNS via notification rules or EventBridge

exp.a: Incorrect. SES is not directly integrated for CodeCommit notifications.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit can send notifications through notification rules (which use SNS topics) or trigger EventBridge rules for events like pushes, pull request creation, and comments.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config tracks resource configuration, not repository events.
exp.d: Incorrect. Kinesis is for streaming data, not repository notifications.

q: What is the relationship between CodePipeline and other AWS services like CodeBuild and CodeDeploy?

opts.b: CodePipeline orchestrates CodeBuild and CodeDeploy as action providers within pipeline stages
opts.c: They are completely independent services with no integration
opts.d: CodeBuild and CodeDeploy are components inside CodePipeline

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline doesn't replace them; it coordinates them.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline acts as the orchestrator, using CodeBuild as a Build/Test action provider and CodeDeploy as a Deploy action provider within its stages.
exp.c: Incorrect. They are deeply integrated.
exp.d: Incorrect. They are separate services that integrate with CodePipeline, not internal components.

q: A team wants their pipeline to deploy to a staging environment first, require approval, and then deploy to production. How many stages should they configure (minimum)?

opts.b: 3 stages

exp.a: Incorrect. 2 stages are insufficient for this workflow.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 stages don't cover all requirements (source + staging + approval + production).
exp.c: Correct. You need Source (get code), Deploy-Staging (deploy to staging), Approval (manual gate), and Deploy-Production (deploy to prod). Note: you may also include a Build stage, making it 5, but the minimum for this workflow is 4.
exp.d: Incorrect. While 5 stages (with Build) is common, 4 is the minimum for the described workflow.

q: Which of the following is a valid CodeDeploy deployment type for Lambda functions?

opts.b: Blue/Green

exp.a: Incorrect. In-place deployment is only for EC2/on-premises.
exp.b: Correct. Lambda deployments use the Blue/Green deployment type, with traffic shifting options like Canary, Linear, or AllAtOnce.
exp.c: Incorrect. Rolling is not a CodeDeploy deployment type.
exp.d: Incorrect. Canary is a traffic routing configuration within Blue/Green, not a deployment type itself.

q: A team is deploying a containerized application to Amazon ECS using CodeDeploy. Which deployment type does CodeDeploy use for ECS?

opts.b: Blue/Green

exp.a: Incorrect. In-place is not available for ECS deployments via CodeDeploy.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy uses Blue/Green deployment for ECS, creating a new task set (green) alongside the original (blue) and shifting traffic between them.
exp.c: Incorrect. Rolling update is an ECS native deployment type, not CodeDeploy's approach.
exp.d: Incorrect. Immutable is an Elastic Beanstalk concept.

q: Where can CodeBuild build logs be stored?

opts.b: Amazon CloudWatch Logs and/or Amazon S3

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 is one option, but not the only one.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild can send build logs to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or both. You configure this in the project's logs configuration.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 is also a valid destination.
exp.d: Incorrect. DynamoDB is not used for build logs.

q: What protocol does CodeCommit use for Git operations over the network?

opts.b: SSH and HTTPS

exp.a: Incorrect. FTP is not used for Git operations.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit supports both SSH (port 22) and HTTPS (port 443) for Git operations.
exp.c: Incorrect. SFTP is not used for CodeCommit.
exp.d: Incorrect. The native Git protocol is not supported by CodeCommit.

q: A CodeBuild project needs to run Docker commands to build container images. The build fails saying 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon'. What setting must be enabled?

opts.b: Privileged mode

exp.a: Incorrect. VPC mode is for accessing private network resources.
exp.b: Correct. Privileged mode must be enabled for CodeBuild to access the Docker daemon. This is required when building Docker images.
exp.c: Incorrect. Batch mode is for running multiple builds.
exp.d: Incorrect. Debug mode doesn't enable Docker access.

q: What is the CodeDeploy agent?

opts.a: A web console for managing deployments
opts.b: A software package that runs on EC2/on-premises instances enabling them to be used as deployment targets
opts.d: A Lambda function that processes deployments

exp.a: Incorrect. The agent is not a web console.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeDeploy agent is a software package installed on EC2/on-premises instances that communicates with CodeDeploy to execute deployments, run lifecycle hook scripts, and report status.
exp.c: Incorrect. It's a standalone agent, not a CLI plugin.
exp.d: Incorrect. It's an agent running on instances, not a Lambda function.

q: A team wants to use CodeCommit but their developers are already familiar with Git commands. Do they need to learn new commands?

opts.b: No, CodeCommit is Git-based and supports all standard Git commands (push, pull, clone, branch, etc.)
opts.c: Only AWS CLI commands work with CodeCommit
opts.d: They need to use the AWS Console only

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit uses standard Git, not proprietary commands.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit is a Git-based repository service. Developers use standard Git commands and any Git client (command line, IDE plugins, etc.) to interact with it.
exp.c: Incorrect. Standard Git commands work; AWS CLI is optional for administrative tasks.
exp.d: Incorrect. While the Console works, Git CLI and other tools are fully supported.

q: Which CodeDeploy hook is the last to run and is typically used to verify the deployment was successful?

opts.b: ApplicationStart

exp.a: Incorrect. AfterInstall runs after installation but before application start.
exp.b: Incorrect. ApplicationStart runs before ValidateService.
exp.c: Correct. ValidateService is the last lifecycle hook in an in-place deployment, used to verify the deployment completed successfully (e.g., checking health endpoints).
exp.d: Incorrect. BeforeInstall is one of the first hooks to run.

q: A company wants to run automated security scanning as part of their pipeline after the build stage but before deployment. Where should they add this in CodePipeline?

opts.b: As a Test stage between Build and Deploy using CodeBuild or a third-party tool
opts.c: In the Deploy stage after deployment

exp.a: Incorrect. Source stage only retrieves code.
exp.b: Correct. A Test stage (using CodeBuild or third-party integrations like Snyk or Checkmarx) between Build and Deploy ensures security issues are caught before deployment.
exp.c: Incorrect. Running security scans after deployment doesn't prevent deploying vulnerable code.
exp.d: Incorrect. Post-deployment scanning is reactive, not preventive.

q: Can CodeBuild run builds on ARM-based processors?

opts.a: No, only x86 processors are supported
opts.b: Yes, CodeBuild supports both x86 and ARM (Graviton) processors

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild supports ARM processors.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild supports ARM-based builds using AWS Graviton processors, which can provide cost savings for compatible workloads.
exp.c: Incorrect. ARM support is for the build environment, not limited to Lambda.
exp.d: Incorrect. AWS provides managed ARM-based images.

q: A developer accidentally deleted a branch in CodeCommit. Can it be recovered?

opts.a: No, deleted branches are permanently lost
opts.b: Yes, using the AWS CLI or Console if you know the commit ID; the commits still exist in the repository
opts.c: Only if there was a backup to S3

exp.a: Incorrect. The branch pointer is deleted but commits remain.
exp.b: Correct. In Git (and CodeCommit), deleting a branch only removes the branch pointer. The commits still exist and a branch can be recreated pointing to the same commit ID using create-branch.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 backups are not required for branch recovery.
exp.d: Incorrect. Recovery can be done by the user without AWS Support.

q: What encryption does CodePipeline use for artifacts stored in S3?

opts.b: Server-side encryption using AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) with either AWS managed key or customer managed key

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline always encrypts artifacts.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline encrypts artifacts in S3 using AWS KMS. By default it uses the AWS managed key (aws/s3), but you can specify a customer managed CMK.
exp.c: Incorrect. Encryption is server-side in S3.
exp.d: Incorrect. SSL/TLS protects data in transit; S3 encryption protects data at rest.

q: A team uses CodePipeline with GitHub as the source. They want the pipeline to trigger only on tags (not every push). Which pipeline type supports this?

opts.b: V2 type pipeline with trigger filters for tags
opts.c: Neither V1 nor V2 supports tag-based triggers
opts.d: Both V1 and V2 support tag-based triggers

exp.a: Incorrect. V1 type doesn't support tag-based trigger filtering.
exp.b: Correct. V2 type pipelines support trigger filters that can be configured to trigger only on specific Git tags, branches, or file paths.
exp.c: Incorrect. V2 does support tag-based triggers.
exp.d: Incorrect. Only V2 supports this feature.

q: How does CodeDeploy determine the order of lifecycle hooks for an in-place deployment?

opts.b: Fixed predefined order: ApplicationStop → DownloadBundle → BeforeInstall → Install → AfterInstall → ApplicationStart → ValidateService

exp.a: Incorrect. The order is not alphabetical.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy follows a strict predefined lifecycle event order. You cannot change the order of hooks.
exp.c: Incorrect. The order is fixed by CodeDeploy, not customizable.
exp.d: Incorrect. The order is deterministic, not random.

q: A team is using CodeBuild and wants to test their application against multiple versions of Node.js (14, 16, 18) simultaneously. What feature should they use?

opts.b: CodeBuild batch builds with build-matrix using different environment variables for each Node.js version
opts.d: Parallel phases in a single build

exp.a: Incorrect. Multiple buildspec files don't enable parallel testing.
exp.b: Correct. Batch builds with build-matrix allow you to define a matrix of environment variables (e.g., NODE_VERSION: [14, 16, 18]) that spawn parallel builds with different configurations.
exp.c: Incorrect. While possible, separate projects add management overhead; batch builds are more elegant.
exp.d: Incorrect. Phases run sequentially within a build; they can't parallelize different environments.

q: What is the maximum number of CodePipeline action executions that can run in parallel within a single stage?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 5.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. A stage can contain up to 50 actions, and actions with the same run order execute in parallel.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a 50-action per stage limit.

q: A company's CodeDeploy deployment to EC2 keeps failing at the AfterInstall hook. The hook script checks if the application started correctly. What should the team investigate?

opts.b: The hook script logic, permissions, and the application's startup behavior at that point in the lifecycle

exp.a: Incorrect. Agent version is rarely the cause of hook-specific failures.
exp.b: Correct. AfterInstall hook failures indicate issues with the script itself (permissions, logic errors) or that the application hasn't fully started yet at that lifecycle stage. ApplicationStart comes after AfterInstall.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 permissions affect artifact download, which happens before AfterInstall.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodePipeline service role isn't involved in hook execution on instances.

q: What CodeBuild feature allows you to interact with a running build session for debugging purposes?

opts.b: Session Manager integration (AWS CodeBuild local debugging)

exp.a: Incorrect. Logs provide passive information, not interactive debugging.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild supports Session Manager integration that allows you to pause a build and open an interactive session to the build environment for debugging.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch provides metrics and logs but not interactive debugging.
exp.d: Incorrect. Direct SSH is not supported; Session Manager provides this capability.

q: A team notices that their CodePipeline artifact S3 bucket is growing very large over time. What should they do?

opts.b: Configure S3 lifecycle rules to automatically expire old pipeline artifacts after a specified period
opts.c: Increase the S3 bucket size limit
opts.d: Move to a different region with more storage

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual deletion is not scalable or reliable.
exp.b: Correct. S3 lifecycle policies can automatically delete or transition old pipeline artifacts to cheaper storage tiers after a specified number of days.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 doesn't have a bucket size limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. Changing regions doesn't address storage growth.

q: Can CodePipeline invoke an AWS Lambda function as an action?

opts.a: No, Lambda cannot be used in CodePipeline
opts.b: Yes, Lambda can be used as an Invoke action for custom logic

exp.a: Incorrect. Lambda is a supported action provider.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline supports Lambda as an Invoke action, allowing you to run custom code (validation, notifications, resource manipulation) as part of the pipeline.
exp.c: Incorrect. Lambda is not a source action.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda is categorized as an Invoke action, not a deploy action.

q: A team's CodeBuild project is in a VPC and needs to pull Docker base images from Docker Hub. The build times out trying to download images. What is the solution?

opts.b: Ensure the VPC subnet has a route to a NAT Gateway for internet access

exp.a: Incorrect. While ECR is recommended, Docker Hub should still be accessible with proper networking.
exp.b: Correct. When CodeBuild is in a VPC, it needs a route to the internet (via NAT Gateway) to access external resources like Docker Hub.
exp.c: Incorrect. Disabling VPC might break other connectivity requirements.
exp.d: Incorrect. Increasing timeout doesn't solve the network connectivity issue.

q: What is the purpose of CodeDeploy's 'minimum healthy hosts' setting?

opts.a: It defines the minimum EC2 instance size
opts.b: It specifies the minimum number or percentage of instances that must remain healthy during deployment
opts.c: It sets the health check interval
opts.d: It defines the minimum memory for the application

exp.a: Incorrect. Instance size is not related to minimum healthy hosts.
exp.b: Correct. Minimum healthy hosts defines how many instances must remain in a healthy state during deployment. If the number drops below this threshold, the deployment fails.
exp.c: Incorrect. Health check intervals are configured elsewhere.
exp.d: Incorrect. Application memory is not related to this setting.

q: Your CodePipeline has a Build stage using CodeBuild that produces a .zip artifact. The Deploy stage uses CodeDeploy but reports 'artifact not found'. What could be wrong?

opts.b: The output artifact name in the Build stage doesn't match the input artifact name configured in the Deploy stage
opts.c: The pipeline is in the wrong region

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeDeploy supports .zip artifacts.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline requires output artifact names from one stage to match input artifact names in the consuming stage. A mismatch causes 'artifact not found' errors.
exp.c: Incorrect. Region mismatch would cause different errors.
exp.d: Incorrect. Both .zip and .tar are supported.

q: How many active users are included in the CodeCommit free tier?

exp.a: Incorrect. The free tier includes more than 1 user.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 is below the actual free tier allowance.
exp.c: Correct. The CodeCommit free tier includes 5 active users per month with 50 GB storage and 10,000 Git requests.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 exceeds the free tier allowance.

q: A team wants to deploy the same application revision to both their staging and production deployment groups. Can they do this in CodeDeploy?

opts.a: No, each deployment group requires a unique revision
opts.b: Yes, the same revision can be deployed to multiple deployment groups within the same application
opts.c: Only if the instances are in the same Auto Scaling group

exp.a: Incorrect. Revisions can be reused across deployment groups.
exp.b: Correct. A single application revision can be deployed to multiple deployment groups (e.g., staging and production) within the same CodeDeploy application.
exp.c: Incorrect. Deployment groups can target different instances or ASGs.
exp.d: Incorrect. Multiple deployment groups within one application can share revisions.

q: What is the free tier for CodeBuild?

opts.b: 100 build minutes per month for general1.small instance

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild does have a free tier.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeBuild free tier includes 100 build minutes per month for the general1.small compute type.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,000 minutes exceeds the free tier.
exp.d: Incorrect. The free tier is time-based, not build-count-based.

q: A new team member cannot clone a CodeCommit repository. They can access the AWS Console. What is the most likely issue?

opts.b: They haven't set up Git credentials (SSH key or HTTPS credentials) in their IAM user settings

exp.a: Incorrect. Repository capacity wouldn't prevent cloning.
exp.b: Correct. To clone via command line, users need either SSH keys uploaded to IAM, HTTPS Git credentials generated in IAM, or the credential helper configured with their AWS credentials.
exp.c: Incorrect. If they can access the Console, CodeCommit is likely available.
exp.d: Incorrect. If it were nonexistent, they wouldn't see it in the Console.

q: Can CodePipeline deploy to AWS Elastic Beanstalk?

opts.a: No, Elastic Beanstalk has its own deployment mechanism
opts.b: Yes, Elastic Beanstalk is a supported deploy action provider in CodePipeline

exp.a: Incorrect. Elastic Beanstalk integrates directly with CodePipeline.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a supported deploy action provider in CodePipeline, allowing direct deployment to Beanstalk environments.
exp.c: Incorrect. Direct Elastic Beanstalk integration exists.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeDeploy is a separate deployment path.

q: A CodeBuild build succeeds but the post_build phase shows warnings. Does the build still count as successful?

opts.a: No, any warnings cause the build to fail
opts.b: Yes, the build status depends on the exit codes of commands in the build phase; post_build runs regardless of the build phase result
opts.c: Only if all warnings are suppressed
opts.d: It depends on the compute type

exp.a: Incorrect. Warnings don't automatically fail a build.
exp.b: Correct. The build phase's exit code determines success or failure. The post_build phase runs regardless (even if build phase fails) and warnings in post_build don't change the overall build status unless commands return non-zero exit codes.
exp.c: Incorrect. Warning suppression isn't required.
exp.d: Incorrect. Compute type doesn't affect build status determination.

q: What is the free tier for CodePipeline V1 type?

opts.b: 1 free active pipeline per month forever

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline V1 does have a free tier.
exp.b: Correct. AWS offers 1 free active V1 type pipeline per month. Additional pipelines are charged at $1 per active pipeline per month.
exp.c: Incorrect. Only 1 pipeline is free.
exp.d: Incorrect. The free tier for CodePipeline is perpetual, not limited to 12 months.
